title.zh: 卷二百〇一 列傳第八十八: 列女二
title.raw: 卷二百〇一 列傳第八十八: 列女二 Volume 201 Biographies 88: Exemplary Women 2

sentences.zh: 武用妻蘇氏，真定人，徙家京師。

translations.literal: Wu Yong's wife, Lady Su, was a person of Zhending; [her family] moved their residence to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yong's wife, Lady Su, came from Zhending; the family later moved to the capital.

sentences.zh: 用疾，蘇氏刲股為粥以進，疾即愈。

translations.literal: Yong fell ill; Lady Su cut flesh from her thigh to make gruel and presented it; the illness then immediately healed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong fell sick, Lady Su sliced flesh from her own thigh to prepare porridge for him, and he soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 生子德政，四歲而寡。

translations.literal: She bore a son, Dezheng; at four [years] she became a widow.
translations.idiomatic: She gave birth to a son named Dezheng and was widowed when the boy was four.

sentences.zh: 夫之兄利其資，欲逼而嫁之，不聽。

translations.literal: Her husband's elder brother coveted her property and wished to force her to remarry; she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's older brother wanted her wealth and tried to pressure her into marrying again, but she refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾夫兄舉家死，惟餘三弱孫，蘇氏取而育之。

translations.literal: Before long the husband's brother's whole household died; only three weak grandsons remained; Lady Su took them and raised them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward her brother-in-law's entire family perished, leaving only three frail grandsons, whom Lady Su took in and reared.

sentences.zh: 德政長，事蘇氏至孝。

translations.literal: Dezheng grew up and served Lady Su with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezheng came of age, he treated Lady Su with the utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 蘇氏死時，天大旱，德政方掘地求水以供葬事，忽二蛇躍出，德政因默禱焉。

translations.literal: When Lady Su died, the sky was greatly drought-stricken; Dezheng was just digging the earth seeking water to supply the burial affairs; suddenly two serpents leaped out; Dezheng thereupon silently prayed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Su died during a severe drought. While Dezheng was digging for water for her funeral, two snakes suddenly sprang from the ground, and he prayed to them in silence.

sentences.zh: 二蛇一東一北，隨其地掘之，果得泉。

translations.literal: The two serpents, one [going] east and one north—following their directions in digging—indeed obtained a spring.
translations.idiomatic: One snake went east and the other north; he dug where they led and found a spring.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事。

translations.literal: The officials reported this matter upward.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported the affair to the court.

sentences.zh: 旌復其家。

translations.literal: [They] commended and exempted her household [from corvée and taxes].
translations.idiomatic: The court honored the family and granted it tax relief.

sentences.zh: 任仲文妻林氏，寧海人。

translations.literal: Ren Zhongwen's wife, Lady Lin, was a person of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhongwen's wife, Lady Lin, was from Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧，年二十八而寡。

translations.literal: The family was very poor; at age twenty-eight she became a widow.
translations.idiomatic: Her household was desperately poor, and she was widowed at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 姑患風疾，不良於行，林氏旦暮扶侍惟謹，撫育三子皆有成。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law suffered from wind ailment and was unfit for walking; Lady Lin morning and evening supported and attended her with sole care; she reared three sons, all achieving success.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law had rheumatism and could barely walk; Lady Lin tended her day and night with scrupulous care, raised three sons, and saw each of them succeed.

sentences.zh: 年一百三歲而卒。

translations.literal: At age one hundred three she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of one hundred and three.

sentences.zh: 江文鑄妻范氏，名妙元，奉化人，年二十一歸於江。

translations.literal: Jiang Wenzhu's wife, Lady Fan, named Miaoyuan, was a person of Fenghua; at age twenty-one she entered the Jiang [household as bride].
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wenzhu's wife, Lady Fan, whose given name was Miaoyuan, came from Fenghua and married into the Jiang family at twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 及門，未合卺，夫忽以蒐疾卒。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the gate, before the wedding cups were joined, the husband suddenly died of sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: She had barely arrived at the door when, before the wedding rites were completed, her husband suddenly died of a sudden illness.

sentences.zh: 範曰；

translations.literal: Fan said:
translations.idiomatic: Fan said:

sentences.zh: 「我既入江氏之門，即江氏婦也，豈以夫亡有異志哉！」

translations.literal: "Since I have already entered the gate of the Jiang clan, I am already a Jiang wife—how could I, because my husband has died, harbor a different intent!"
translations.idiomatic: "I have already entered the Jiang household and am a Jiang wife. How could the death of my husband change my resolve?"

sentences.zh: 遂居江氏之家，撫諸侄江森、江道如己子。

translations.literal: Thereupon she dwelt in the Jiang household and reared the nephews Jiang Sen and Jiang Dao as her own sons.
translations.idiomatic: She remained in the Jiang home and raised her nephews Jiang Sen and Jiang Dao as if they were her own children.

sentences.zh: 卒年九十五。

translations.literal: At death she was ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: She died at ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 有柳氏者，蘇郡人，為戶部主事趙野妻。

translations.literal: There was a Lady Liu, a person of Su Prefecture, who was wife of Zhao Ye, a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Lady Liu from Suzhou, wife of Zhao Ye, a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 未示成婚而野卒，柳哭之盡哀，誓不再嫁。

translations.literal: Before the wedding ceremony was performed, Ye died; Liu wept for him with utmost grief and vowed never to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding could take place, Zhao Ye died. Liu mourned him with deepest grief and swore never to marry again.

sentences.zh: 其兄將奪其志，柳曰：「業已歸趙氏，雖未成婚，而夫婦之禮已定矣。

translations.literal: Her elder brother was about to wrest away her resolve; Liu said: "I have already been betrothed to the Zhao clan; although the wedding has not yet been performed, the rites of husband and wife are already fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When her brother tried to make her change her mind, Liu said, "I have already been pledged to the Zhao family. Though we never wed, the bond of husband and wife was already settled.

sentences.zh: 雖凍餓死，豈有他志哉！」

translations.literal: Even if I freeze or starve to death, how could I have another intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I freeze or starve to death, I could never think otherwise!"

sentences.zh: 后寢疾，不肯服藥，曰： 「我年二十六而寡，今已逾半百，得死此疾幸矣。」

translations.literal: Later she took to bed with illness, refused to take medicine, and said: "I was widowed at twenty-six; now I have already passed half a century—to die of this illness is fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Later she fell ill and refused medicine, saying, "I was widowed at twenty-six and am now past fifty. To die of this illness would be a blessing."

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon she died.
translations.idiomatic: And so she died.

sentences.zh: 姚氏，餘杭人，居山谷間。

translations.literal: Lady Yao, a person of Yuhang, dwelt in a mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yao of Yuhang lived in a mountain valley.

sentences.zh: 夫出刈麥，姚居家執爨。

translations.literal: Her husband went out to reap wheat; Yao remained at home tending the cooking.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband went out to harvest wheat while she stayed home to cook.

sentences.zh: 母何氏往汲澗水，久而不至。

translations.literal: Her mother, Lady He, went to draw water from the stream ravine; long she did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law, Lady He, went to fetch water from the brook and was gone a long time.

sentences.zh: 俄聞覆水聲，亟出視，則虎銜其母以走。

translations.literal: Suddenly she heard the sound of overturned water; she hurried out to look—and a tiger was holding her mother-in-law in its jaws and running off.
translations.idiomatic: She suddenly heard a splash, rushed outside, and saw a tiger carrying her mother-in-law away in its mouth.

sentences.zh: 姚倉卒往逐之，即以手毆其脅，鄰人競執器械以從，虎乃置之而去。

translations.literal: Yao in haste went to pursue it; immediately with her hands she struck its flank; neighbors all vied to take up weapons and follow; the tiger then released [her] and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao rushed after the tiger and beat its flank with her bare hands; neighbors seized weapons and joined the chase, and the tiger dropped her mother-in-law and fled.

sentences.zh: 姚負母以歸，求藥療之，奉養二十餘年而卒。

translations.literal: Yao carried her mother-in-law back on her back, sought medicine to treat her, and attended her for more than twenty years until she died.
translations.idiomatic: Yao carried her mother-in-law home, nursed her with medicine, and cared for her for more than twenty years until her death.

sentences.zh: 又方寧妻官勝娘者，建寧人。

translations.literal: Also Fang Ning's wife, Guan Shengniang, was a person of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Guan Shengniang of Jianning, wife of Fang Ning.

sentences.zh: 寧耨田，勝娘饁之，見一虎方攫其夫，勝娘即棄饁奮梃連擊之，虎捨去，勝娘負夫至中途而死。

translations.literal: Ning was hoeing the fields; Shengniang brought him food; she saw a tiger just seizing her husband; Shengniang immediately cast aside the food, seized a club, and struck it repeatedly; the tiger released him; Shengniang carried her husband on her back; midway he died.
translations.idiomatic: While Ning was hoeing his field, Shengniang brought him lunch and saw a tiger seizing him. She dropped the food, grabbed a club, and beat the tiger until it let go. She carried her husband away, but he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，為旌復其家。

translations.literal: The officials reported it upward; [the court] commended and exempted her household.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported the matter, and the court honored her family with commendation and tax relief.

sentences.zh: 衣氏，汴梁儒士孟志剛妻。

translations.literal: Lady Yi was wife of Meng Zhigang, a Confucian scholar of Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yi was the wife of Meng Zhigang, a scholar of Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 志剛卒，貧而無子，有司給以棺木。

translations.literal: Zhigang died; [they were] poor and without sons; the officials supplied a coffin and wood.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigang died, they were poor and childless, and the authorities provided a coffin.

sentences.zh: 衣氏紿匠者曰：「可寬大其棺，吾夫有遺衣服，欲盡置其中。」

translations.literal: Lady Yi deceived the craftsman, saying: "You may make the coffin wide and large; my husband has leftover clothes that I wish to place entirely within it."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yi told the carpenter, "Make the coffin larger. My husband left clothes that I want to place inside with him."

sentences.zh: 匠者然之。

translations.literal: The craftsman assented.
translations.idiomatic: The carpenter agreed.

sentences.zh: 是夕，衣氏具雞黍祭其夫，家之所有悉散之鄰里及同居王媼，曰：「吾聞一馬不被兩鞍，吾夫既死，與之同棺共穴可也。」

translations.literal: That evening, Lady Yi prepared chicken and millet to sacrifice to her husband; everything the household possessed she entirely distributed to neighbors and to Old Woman Wang who lived together [with them], saying: "I have heard that one horse does not bear two saddles; since my husband is dead, to share one coffin and one grave with him is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: That night she prepared a meal to honor her husband and gave away everything they owned to the neighbors and to Old Woman Wang, who lived with them, saying, "They say one horse cannot bear two saddles. Now that my husband is dead, it is right that we share one coffin and one grave."

sentences.zh: 遂自剄死。

translations.literal: Thereupon she cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then she cut her own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 有侯氏者，鈞州曹德妻。

translations.literal: There was a Lady Hou, wife of Cao De of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: There was Lady Hou, wife of Cao De of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 德病死，侯氏語人曰：「年少夫亡，婦人之不幸也。

translations.literal: De died of illness; Lady Hou told people: "To lose one's husband while young is a woman's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: When De died of illness, Lady Hou said to others, "To lose one's husband while still young is a woman's greatest misfortune.

sentences.zh: 欲守吾志，而亂離如​​此，其能免乎！」

translations.literal: I wished to keep my resolve, yet chaos and separation are like this—how could one escape it!"
translations.idiomatic: I wished to keep my vow, but with chaos and upheaval like this, how could I hope to remain untouched?"

sentences.zh: 遂縊死於墓。

translations.literal: Thereupon she hanged herself at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Then she hanged herself at his grave.

sentences.zh: 又周經妻吳氏、郭惟辛妻郝氏、陳輝妻白氏、張頑住妻杜氏、程二妻成氏、李貞妻武氏、暗都剌妻張氏，並以夫死，不忍獨生，自縊而死。

translations.literal: Also Zhou Jing's wife Lady Wu, Guo Weixin's wife Lady Hao, Chen Hui's wife Lady Bai, Zhang Wanzhu's wife Lady Du, Cheng Er's wife Lady Cheng, Li Zhen's wife Lady Wu, and Andula's wife Lady Zhang—all because their husbands died, could not bear to live alone, and hanged themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu, wife of Zhou Jing; Lady Hao, wife of Guo Weixin; Lady Bai, wife of Chen Hui; Lady Du, wife of Zhang Wanzhu; Lady Cheng, wife of Cheng Er; Lady Wu, wife of Li Zhen; and Lady Zhang, wife of Andula—all hanged themselves when their husbands died, unwilling to live on alone.

sentences.zh: 事聞，咸旌異之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, all were commended with special distinction.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, each was honored with special commendation.

sentences.zh: 湯輝妻張氏，處州龍泉人。

translations.literal: Tang Hui's wife, Lady Zhang, was a person of Longquan in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Hui's wife, Lady Zhang, was from Longquan in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會兵亂，其家財先已移入山寨，夫與姑共守之。

translations.literal: When military chaos arose, their household property had already been moved into a mountain stockade; husband and mother-in-law together guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out, the family had already moved their valuables into a mountain fort, where her husband and mother-in-law stayed to guard them.

sentences.zh: 舅以疾未行，張歸任藥膳，且以輿自隨。

translations.literal: Her father-in-law's younger brother, because of illness, had not gone; Zhang returned to attend to medicines and food, and moreover had a sedan chair follow her of her own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's uncle was too ill to travel, so Zhang went back to prepare his medicine and meals and brought a sedan chair with her.

sentences.zh: 既而賊至，即命以輿載其舅，而己遇賊。

translations.literal: Before long bandits arrived; she immediately ordered that the sedan chair carry her uncle, while she herself encountered the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits arrived, she ordered the sedan bearers to carry her uncle away while she herself faced the raiders.

sentences.zh: 賊以刀脅之曰：「從我則生，否則死。」

translations.literal: The bandits threatened her with blades, saying: "Follow us and you live; otherwise you die."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits held blades to her and said, "Come with us and live, or refuse and die."

sentences.zh: 張掠發整衣請受刃，賊未忍殺，張懼污，即奪其刃自剚死，年二十七。

translations.literal: Zhang tossed back her hair, straightened her garments, and asked to receive the blade; the bandits could not bear to kill her; Zhang feared defilement and immediately seized their blade and stabbed herself to death; she was twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang tossed her hair aside, straightened her clothes, and asked them to strike. The bandits hesitated, so fearing dishonor she seized a blade and stabbed herself to death. She was twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 又湯婍者，亦龍泉人，有姿容。

translations.literal: Also Tang Qi was likewise a person of Longquan and had beauty of appearance.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Tang Qi of Longquan, a woman of striking beauty.

sentences.zh: 賊殺其父母，以刃脅之。

translations.literal: Bandits killed her parents and threatened her with blades.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits killed her parents and threatened her with blades.

sentences.zh: 婍不勝悲咽，乞早死，因以頭觸刃。

translations.literal: Qi could not bear the grief and choking sobs; she begged for early death and thereupon struck the blade with her head.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with grief, Qi begged to die quickly and thrust her head against the blade.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，斫殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits grew angry and hacked her to death.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits hacked her to death.

sentences.zh: 其妹亦不受辱而死。

translations.literal: Her younger sister likewise would not accept dishonor and died.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger sister likewise chose death rather than submit to dishonor.

sentences.zh: 俞士淵妻童氏，嚴州人。

translations.literal: Yu Shiyuan's wife, Lady Tong, was a person of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiyuan's wife, Lady Tong, was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 姑性嚴，待之寡恩，童氏柔順以事之，無少拂其意者。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law was stern in nature and treated her with little kindness; Lady Tong with gentle compliance served her, never in the least going against her wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was severe and showed her little kindness, yet Lady Tong served her with gentle obedience and never once crossed her.

sentences.zh: 至正十三年，賊陷威平，官軍復之，已乃縱兵剽掠。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhizheng, bandits captured Weiping; government troops recovered it, and afterward let the soldiers plunder freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhizheng, rebels seized Weiping. After government troops retook the city, the soldiers were allowed to loot freely.

sentences.zh: 至士淵家，童氏以身蔽姑。

translations.literal: When they reached Shiyuan's home, Lady Tong used her body to shield her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When the soldiers came to Shiyuan's home, Lady Tong shielded her mother-in-law with her own body.

sentences.zh: 眾欲污之，童氏大罵不屈。

translations.literal: The crowd wished to defile her; Lady Tong reviled them loudly and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to violate her, but Lady Tong cursed them loudly and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 一卒以刀擊其左臂，愈不屈。

translations.literal: One soldier struck her left arm with a blade; she yielded all the less.
translations.idiomatic: One soldier slashed her left arm, yet she yielded all the more stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 又一卒斷其右臂，罵猶不絕。

translations.literal: Another soldier severed her right arm; her curses still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Another cut off her right arm, yet her curses never stopped.

sentences.zh: 眾乃皮其面而去，明日乃死。

translations.literal: The crowd then flayed her face and departed; the next day she died.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers flayed her face and left; she died the next day.

sentences.zh: 張氏女，高郵人。

translations.literal: The Zhang clan's daughter was a person of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of the Zhang family lived in Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 城亂，賊知張女有姿艷，叩其家索之。

translations.literal: When the city fell into chaos, bandits knew the Zhang daughter had beauty and grace; they knocked at her home demanding her.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was thrown into chaos, bandits learned that the Zhang daughter was beautiful and came to her home demanding her.

sentences.zh: 女方匿复宇間，賊將害其父母，女不得已乃出拜賊。

translations.literal: The girl had just hidden in the space between the roof layers; the bandits were about to harm her parents; the girl had no choice and thereupon came out to bow to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: She had just hidden in the space beneath the eaves when the bandits threatened to kill her parents. With no other choice, she came out and bowed to them.

sentences.zh: 賊即伏地呼其父母為丈人媼，而以女行，女欣欣然從之。

translations.literal: The bandits immediately prostrated themselves on the ground, calling her parents father-in-law and mother-in-law, and then departed with the girl; the girl cheerfully followed them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits prostrated themselves, addressed her parents as father- and mother-in-law, and led the girl away. She followed them with apparent cheer.

sentences.zh: 過橋，投水死。

translations.literal: When they crossed a bridge, she cast herself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to a bridge, she threw herself into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 有高氏婦者，同郡人也。

translations.literal: There was also a wife of the Gao clan, likewise a person of the same prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a woman of the Gao clan from the same region.

sentences.zh: 攜其女從夫出避亂，見道旁空舍，入其中，脫金纏臂與女，且語夫，令疾行。

translations.literal: She took her daughter and followed her husband out to flee the chaos; seeing an empty house by the road, she entered it, removed her gold armlet and gave it to her daughter, and moreover told her husband to go quickly.
translations.idiomatic: She fled the turmoil with her husband and daughter, entered an empty house by the road, removed her gold armlet and gave it to her daughter, and told her husband to hurry on.

sentences.zh: 夫挈女稍遠，乃解足紗自經。

translations.literal: When her husband had led the daughter somewhat farther off, she then untied the foot-binding cloth and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband had taken their daughter a little farther on, she untied her foot bindings and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 賊至，焚其舍。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived, they burned the house.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived, they burned the house down.

sentences.zh: 夫抵儀真，夜夢婦來告曰：「我已縊死彼舍矣。」

translations.literal: Her husband reached Yizhen; at night he dreamed his wife came to tell him: "I have already hanged myself in that house."
translations.idiomatic: When her husband reached Yizhen, he dreamed that night that his wife came to him and said, "I have already hanged myself in that house."

sentences.zh: 其精爽如此。

translations.literal: Her spiritual presence was thus vivid.
translations.idiomatic: Her spirit had been so vivid.

sentences.zh: 惠士玄妻王氏，大都人。

translations.literal: Hui Shixuan's wife, Lady Wang, was a person of Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Hui Shixuan's wife, Lady Wang, was from Dadu.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，士玄病革，王氏曰：「吾聞病者糞苦則愈。」

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, Shixuan's illness became critical; Lady Wang said: "I have heard that when the sick person's stool is bitter, he recovers."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, Shixuan fell gravely ill. Lady Wang said, "I have heard that when a patient's stool tastes bitter, he will recover."

sentences.zh: 乃嘗其糞，頗甘，王氏色愈憂。

translations.literal: Thereupon she tasted his stool; it was rather sweet; Lady Wang's countenance grew all the more troubled.
translations.idiomatic: She tasted his stool and found it rather sweet, and her face grew all the more troubled.

sentences.zh: 士玄囑王氏曰：「我病必不起，前妾所生子，汝善保護之。

translations.literal: Shixuan charged Lady Wang, saying: "My illness certainly will not rise again; the son born by my former concubine—you must protect him well.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan told Lady Wang, "I will not recover. The son born to my former concubine—you must care for him well.

sentences.zh: 待此子稍長，即從汝自嫁矣。」

translations.literal: When this child grows somewhat older, then follow your own wish and remarry."
translations.idiomatic: When he grows a little older, you may remarry as you wish."

sentences.zh: 王氏泣曰：「君何為出此言耶！

translations.literal: Lady Wang wept and said: "My lord, why do you speak such words!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang wept and said, "My lord, why do you speak such words?

sentences.zh: 設有不諱，妾義當死，尚復有他說乎。

translations.literal: If there should be misfortune, by duty I ought to die—how could there still be other talk!
translations.idiomatic: If the worst should come, it is my duty to die with you. What other course could there be?

sentences.zh: 君幸有兄嫂，此兒必不失所居。」

translations.literal: My lord fortunately has elder brother and sister-in-law; this child certainly will not lose his dwelling place."
translations.idiomatic: You still have your brother and sister-in-law; the boy will not be left without a home."

sentences.zh: 數日，士玄卒。

translations.literal: Several days later, Shixuan died.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, Shixuan died.

sentences.zh: 比葬，王氏遂居墓側，蓬首垢面，哀毀逾禮，常以妾子置左右，飲食寒暖惟恐不至。

translations.literal: When the time came for burial, Lady Wang thereupon dwelt beside the tomb, with disheveled hair and filthy face, her grief and emaciation exceeding the rites; she constantly kept the concubine's son at her side, fearing lest food, drink, warmth, or cold should fail to reach him.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral, Lady Wang lived beside the grave with unkempt hair and a filthy face, mourning beyond what ritual required. She kept the concubine's son always at her side and tended his food, drink, warmth, and comfort with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，妾子亦死，乃哭曰：「無復望矣。」

translations.literal: After more than a year, the concubine's son also died; she then wept, saying: "There is no further hope."
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the concubine's son also died. She wept and said, "There is nothing left to hope for."

sentences.zh: 屢引刀自殺。

translations.literal: She repeatedly drew a knife to kill herself.
translations.idiomatic: She tried again and again to kill herself with a knife.

sentences.zh: 家人驚救，得免。

translations.literal: Her family, startled, rescued her; she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Her family rushed to stop her and saved her.

sentences.zh: 至終喪，親舊皆攜酒禮祭士玄於墓。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, relatives and friends all brought wine and ritual offerings to sacrifice to Shixuan at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, relatives and friends brought wine and offerings to honor Shixuan at his grave.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，眾欲行酒，王氏已經死於樹矣。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was finished, the crowd wished to proceed with wine; Lady Wang had already hanged herself from a tree.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites, as everyone prepared to drink together, they found that Lady Wang had already hanged herself from a tree.

sentences.zh: 又有王氏者，良鄉費隱妻也。

translations.literal: There was also a Lady Wang, wife of Fei Yin of Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Wang, wife of Fei Yin of Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 隱有疾，王氏數嘗其糞。

translations.literal: Yin had an illness; Lady Wang repeatedly tasted his stool.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin fell ill, Lady Wang repeatedly tasted his stool to gauge his condition.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，囑王氏曰：「我一子一女，雖妾所生，無異汝所出也。

translations.literal: When the illness became severe, he charged Lady Wang, saying: "I have one son and one daughter; although born by a concubine, they are no different from those you bore.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew critical, he told Lady Wang, "I have a son and a daughter. Though born to a concubine, they are no different from your own children.

sentences.zh: 我死，汝其善撫育之。」

translations.literal: When I die, you must rear them well."
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, you must raise them well."

sentences.zh: 遂歿。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died.

sentences.zh: 王氏居喪，撫其子女。

translations.literal: Lady Wang dwelt in mourning and reared the children.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang mourned him and raised the children.

sentences.zh: 既而子又死。

translations.literal: Before long the son also died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the son died as well.

sentences.zh: 服除，謂其親屬曰：「妾聞夫乃婦之天，今夫已死，妾生何為！」

translations.literal: When the mourning garments were removed, she told her kin, saying: "I have heard that the husband is the wife's heaven; now my husband is dead—why should I, his wife, live!"
translations.idiomatic: When her mourning period ended, she told her relatives, "They say a husband is a wife's heaven. Now that my husband is dead, why should I go on living?"

sentences.zh: 乃執女手，語之曰：「汝今已長，稍知人事，管鑰在此，汝自司之。」

translations.literal: She then took the girl's hand and said to her, "You have grown up now and know a little about the ways of the world. The keys are here—take charge of them yourself."
translations.idiomatic: She then took her daughter's hand and said, "You're grown now and understand something of life. Here are the household keys—manage them yourself."

sentences.zh: 遂相抱慟哭。

translations.literal: Then they embraced each other and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Then mother and daughter held each other and sobbed in grief.

sentences.zh: 是夜，縊死於園中。

translations.literal: That night she hanged herself in the garden.
translations.idiomatic: That same night she hanged herself in the garden.

sentences.zh: 李景文妻徐氏，名彩鸞，字淑和，浦城徐嗣源之女。

translations.literal: Li Jingwen's wife, Lady Xu, named Cailuan, styled Shuhe, was the daughter of Xu Siyuan of Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingwen's wife, Lady Xu—given name Cailuan, courtesy name Shuhe—was Xu Siyuan's daughter of Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 略通經史，每誦文天祥《六歌》，必為之感泣。

translations.literal: She had some knowledge of the classics and histories; whenever she recited Wen Tianxiang's Six Songs, she invariably wept moved by them.
translations.idiomatic: She was versed in the classics and histories, and whenever she read Wen Tianxiang's Six Songs, she was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，青田賊寇浦城，徐氏從嗣源逃旁近山谷。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng, bandits from Qingtian raided Pucheng; Lady Xu fled with Siyuan to a nearby mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 15, Qingtian bandits attacked Pucheng, and Lady Xu fled with her father Siyuan into a nearby valley.

sentences.zh: 賊持刀欲害嗣源，徐氏前曰：「此吾父也，寧殺我。」

translations.literal: The bandits, swords in hand, were about to kill Siyuan; Lady Xu stepped forward and said, "This is my father—kill me instead."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits drew their swords to kill Siyuan, but Lady Xu stepped forward and said, "He is my father—better kill me instead."

sentences.zh: 賊舍父而止徐氏。

translations.literal: The bandits let the father go and seized Lady Xu instead.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits released her father and took Lady Xu in his place.

sentences.zh: 徐氏語父曰：「兒義不受辱，今必死，父可速去。」

translations.literal: Lady Xu told her father, "Your daughter, bound by righteousness, will not accept disgrace—I must die now; father, go quickly."
translations.idiomatic: She told her father, "I cannot live in dishonor. I am going to die—please leave at once."

sentences.zh: 賊拘徐氏至桂林橋，拾炭題詩壁間，有「惟有桂林橋下水，千年照見妾心清」之句。

translations.literal: The bandits held Lady Xu at Guilin Bridge; she picked up charcoal and wrote a poem on the wall, with the line: "Only the waters beneath Guilin Bridge, through a thousand years, mirror clear the heart of this woman."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits took her to Guilin Bridge, where she wrote a poem on the wall with a piece of charcoal, including the line, "Only the waters beneath Guilin Bridge, for a thousand years, will reflect how pure my heart remains."

sentences.zh: 乃厲聲罵賊，投於水。

translations.literal: Thereupon she loudly cursed the bandits and threw herself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: She then denounced the bandits at the top of her voice and threw herself into the river.

sentences.zh: 賊競出之。

translations.literal: The bandits rushed out and pulled her up.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits rushed in and pulled her out.

sentences.zh: 既而乘間復投水死。

translations.literal: Presently, seizing an opportunity, she again threw herself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward she found a moment to jump in again and drowned.

sentences.zh: 周婦毛氏，松陽人，美姿色。

translations.literal: Madame Zhou, née Mao, was a native of Songyang, fair of face.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Zhou household, née Mao, came from Songyang and was renowned for her beauty.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，隨其夫避亂麻鷖山中，為賊所得。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng, she followed her husband in taking refuge from the turmoil on Mayi mountain, where bandits captured her.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 15 she fled with her husband to Mayi mountain to escape the chaos, and bandits seized her there.

sentences.zh: 脅之曰：「從我多與若金，否則殺汝。」

translations.literal: They threatened her, saying, "Follow me and I will give you plenty of gold; otherwise I will kill you."
translations.idiomatic: They threatened her: "Come with me and I'll give you gold; refuse, and you're dead."

sentences.zh: 毛氏曰：「寧剖我心，不願汝金。」

translations.literal: Lady Mao said, "I would rather have my heart cut open than accept your gold."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao replied, "I'd sooner have my heart cut out than take your gold."

sentences.zh: 賊以刀磨其身，毛氏因大詈曰：「碎呙賊，汝碎則臭，我碎則香。」

translations.literal: The bandits whetted a blade against her body; Lady Mao thereupon cursed them loudly, saying, "Bandit scum! If you are smashed, you stink; if I am smashed, I am fragrant."
translations.idiomatic: A bandit scraped a knife along her body. She cried out, "You bandit scum! Smash you and you'd reek; smash me and I'd still smell sweet."

sentences.zh: 賊怒，刳其腸而去，年二十九。

translations.literal: In fury the bandits disemboweled her and left; she was twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they cut out her bowels and left her to die. She was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 丁尚賢妻李氏，汴梁人。

translations.literal: Ding Shangxian's wife, Lady Li, was a native of Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shangxian's wife, Lady Li, came from Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，有姿容。

translations.literal: She was a little over twenty and comely in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: She was in her twenties and attractive.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，賊至，欲虜之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng, when bandits arrived, they sought to seize her.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 15, when bandits came, they tried to capture her.

sentences.zh: 李氏怒曰：「吾家六世義門，豈能從賊以辱身乎！」

translations.literal: Lady Li said angrily, "Our house is a six-generation hall of righteousness—how could I follow bandits and disgrace myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li furiously declared, "Our family has been a righteous household for six generations—I will never follow bandits and bring shame on myself!"

sentences.zh: 於是闔門三百餘口俱被害。

translations.literal: Thereupon the entire household—more than three hundred people—were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then slaughtered the entire household, more than three hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 李順兒者，許州儒士李讓之女也。

translations.literal: Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a Confucian scholar of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun'er was the daughter of Li Rang, a scholar of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 性聰慧，頗涉經傳，年十八，未嫁。

translations.literal: By nature clever, she had dipped into the classics and commentaries; she was eighteen and unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent and well read in the classics, she was eighteen and still unmarried.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，賊陷鈞州，密邇許昌。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng, bandits captured Junzhou, close by Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 15 rebels took Junzhou, right next to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 父謂其母曰：「吾家以詩禮相傳，此女必累我。」

translations.literal: Her father said to her mother, "Our family has handed down poetry and ritual; this girl will surely be our ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Her father told her mother, "Our family lives by poetry and ritual—this daughter will bring disaster on us."

sentences.zh: 女聞之，泣曰：「父母可自逃難，勿以我為憂。」

translations.literal: The girl heard this and wept, saying, "Father and mother, flee for your lives yourselves—do not grieve over me."
translations.idiomatic: Overhearing, she wept and said, "Mother and Father, save yourselves—do not worry about me."

sentences.zh: 須臾於後園內自經而死。

translations.literal: In a little while she hanged herself in the rear garden and died.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later she hanged herself in the back garden.

sentences.zh: 吳守正妻禹氏，名淑靜，字素清，紹興人。

translations.literal: Wu Shouzheng's wife, Lady Yu, named Shujing, styled Suqing, was a native of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shouzheng's wife, Lady Yu—given name Shujing, courtesy name Suqing—was from Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 至正十六年，徙家崇德之石門。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, the family moved to Shimen in Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 16 the family resettled at Shimen in Chongde.

sentences.zh: 淑靜嘗從容謂守正曰：「方今群盜蜂起，萬一不測，妾惟有死而已，不使人污此身也。」

translations.literal: Shujing once calmly said to Shouzheng, "Nowadays bandits rise everywhere like swarming bees; if anything unforeseen should happen, I can only choose death—I will not let anyone defile this body."
translations.idiomatic: Shujing once told Shouzheng calmly, "Thieves are rising everywhere. If the worst should happen, death is my only choice—I won't let anyone dishonor me."

sentences.zh: 是年夏，盜陷崇德，淑靜倉皇攜八歲女登舟以避。

translations.literal: That summer, bandits seized Chongde; Shujing hurriedly boarded a boat with her eight-year-old daughter to escape.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Chongde fell. Shujing fled in panic onto a boat with her eight-year-old daughter.

sentences.zh: 有盜數輩奔入其舟，將犯淑靜，淑靜乃抱幼女投河死。

translations.literal: Several bandits rushed into the boat and were about to violate Shujing; Shujing then embraced her young daughter and leaped into the river to her death.
translations.idiomatic: Several bandits stormed the boat and moved to assault her. Shujing clutched her daughter and leaped into the river, drowning them both.

sentences.zh: 黃仲起妻朱氏，杭州人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhongqi's wife, Lady Zhu, was a native of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhongqi's wife, Lady Zhu, came from Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至正十六年，張士誠寇杭州，其女臨安奴倉皇言曰：「賊至矣，我別母求一死也。」

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, Zhang Shicheng attacked Hangzhou; his daughter Lin'annu said in alarm, "The bandits are here—I take leave of my mother to seek death."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 16 Zhang Shicheng besieged Hangzhou. His daughter Lin'annu cried out in alarm, "The rebels are here—Mother, forgive me, but I must find a way to die."

sentences.zh: 俄而賊驅諸婦至其家，且指朱氏母子曰：「為我看守，日暮我當至也。」

translations.literal: Soon the bandits drove several women to their house and, pointing at Lady Zhu and her daughter, said, "Keep watch over these for me; at dusk I shall return."
translations.idiomatic: Moments later bandits herded women to the house and told the guards, pointing at Lady Zhu and her daughter, "Watch these two. I'll be back at dusk."

sentences.zh: 朱氏聞之，懼受辱，遂與女俱縊死。

translations.literal: Lady Zhu heard this, feared being dishonored, and hanged herself together with her daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disgrace, Lady Zhu and her daughter hanged themselves together.

sentences.zh: 妾馮氏，見其母子已死，歎曰：「我生何為，徒受辱耳！」

translations.literal: The concubine, Lady Feng, seeing mother and daughter already dead, sighed and said, "Why was I born—only to suffer disgrace in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: The concubine Lady Feng saw them dead and sighed, "What is my life for, if not to be humiliated!"

sentences.zh: 亦自縊死。

translations.literal: She too hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 繼而仲起弟妻蔡氏，抱幼子玄童，與乳母湯氏皆自縊。

translations.literal: Then Zhongqi's younger brother's wife, Lady Cai, holding the infant child Xuantong, together with the wet nurse, Lady Tang, all hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Next Zhongqi's sister-in-law Lady Cai, clutching her infant son Xuantong, along with the wet nurse Lady Tang, also took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 及暮，賊至，見諸屍滿室，執仲起將殺之，哀求得脫。

translations.literal: At dusk the bandits came, saw corpses filling the room, seized Zhongqi and were about to kill him; he pleaded piteously and was released.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits returned at dusk and found corpses strewn through the house, they seized Zhongqi to kill him, but he begged so desperately they let him go.

sentences.zh: 賊遂盡掠其家財而去。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon looted the family's entire wealth and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They stripped the household of everything and left.

sentences.zh: 焦士廉妻王氏，博興人，養姑至孝。

translations.literal: Jiao Shilian's wife, Lady Wang, was a native of Boxing and filially cared for her mother-in-law to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Shilian's wife, Lady Wang, came from Boxing and was deeply filial toward her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 至正十七年，毛貴作亂，官軍競出虜掠。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhizheng, Mao Gui rebelled, and government troops rushed forth in mutual pillaging.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 17 Mao Gui rose in rebellion, and government troops competed in raiding and looting.

sentences.zh: 王氏被執，紿曰：「我家墓田有藏金，可共取也。」

translations.literal: Lady Wang was seized; she deceived them, saying, "Our family's tomb fields have hidden gold—we can go and take it together."
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wang was seized, she lied, "There's hidden gold in our family's burial fields—I'll show you where."

sentences.zh: 信之，隨王氏至墓所。

translations.literal: They believed her and followed Lady Wang to the grave site.
translations.idiomatic: Believing her, they followed her to the graves.

sentences.zh: 王氏哭曰：「我已得死所矣，實無藏金，汝可於此殺我。」

translations.literal: Lady Wang wept and said, "I have already found the place to die; there truly is no hidden gold—you may kill me here."
translations.idiomatic: There she wept and said, "I've found where I want to die. There is no gold—just kill me here."

sentences.zh: 乃與妾杜氏皆遇害。

translations.literal: Thereupon she and the concubine, Lady Du, were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: They killed her and the concubine Lady Du.

sentences.zh: 又有趙氏者，平陽人，年二十，未嫁。

translations.literal: There was also a Lady Zhao, a native of Pingyang, twenty years old and unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: Another was Lady Zhao of Pingyang—twenty, and still unmarried.

sentences.zh: 寇亂，趙被驅迫以行，度不能免​​，紿賊曰：「吾取所藏金以遺汝。」

translations.literal: During the bandit turmoil, Zhao was driven along and marched off; seeing she could not escape, she deceived the bandits, saying, "I will fetch the gold I have hidden and give it to you."
translations.idiomatic: When bandits swept through, Zhao was forced along with them. Realizing she could not escape, she told them, "I'll get the gold I've hidden and give it to you."

sentences.zh: 賊信之，遂​​還，投於廁而死。

translations.literal: The bandits believed her, returned accordingly, and she threw herself into a privy and died.
translations.idiomatic: They believed her and turned back. She threw herself into a latrine and died.

sentences.zh: 陳淑真，富州陳璧之女。

translations.literal: Chen Shuzhen was the daughter of Chen Bi of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuzhen was Chen Bi's daughter of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 璧故儒者，避亂移家龍興。

translations.literal: Bi had formerly been a Confucian scholar; fleeing the turmoil, he moved his family to Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Bi was a scholar who moved the family to Longxing to escape the chaos.

sentences.zh: 淑真七歲能誦詩鼓琴。

translations.literal: At seven Shuzhen could recite poetry and play the zither.
translations.idiomatic: At seven she could recite poetry and play the zither.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，陳友諒寇龍興，淑真見鄰嫗倉皇來告，乃取琴坐牖下彈之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, Chen Youliang attacked Longxing; Shuzhen saw a neighboring woman rush in with the alarm, took her zither, sat beneath the window, and played.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 18 Chen Youliang attacked Longxing. When a neighbor ran in with the news, Shuzhen took her zither, sat by the window, and played.

sentences.zh: 曲終，泫然流涕曰：「吾絕弦於斯乎！」

translations.literal: When the piece ended, she said with tears streaming down, "Shall I break my strings here!"
translations.idiomatic: When the piece ended, she wept and said, "Is this where I break my strings forever?"

sentences.zh: 父母怪，問之，淑真曰：「城陷必遭辱，不如早死。」

translations.literal: Her parents wondered and asked her; Shuzhen said, "When the city falls I am sure to suffer disgrace—better to die early."
translations.idiomatic: Her parents were alarmed and asked what she meant. She said, "When the city falls I'll be dishonored. Better to die now."

sentences.zh: 明日賊至，其居臨東湖，遂溺焉。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits came; her dwelling bordered East Lake, and she drowned herself there.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels arrived. Her home stood by East Lake, and she drowned herself in it.

sentences.zh: 水淺不死，賊抽矢脅之上岸，淑真不從，賊射殺之。

translations.literal: The water was shallow and she did not die; the bandits drew arrows and threatened her to come ashore—Shuzhen refused, and they shot her dead.
translations.idiomatic: The water was too shallow to drown her. Bandits nocked arrows and ordered her ashore, but she refused, and they shot her dead.

sentences.zh: 時同郡李宗頤妻夏氏，名婉常，亦儒家女。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zongyi's wife of the same prefecture, Lady Xia, named Wanchang, was also a daughter of a Confucian family.
translations.idiomatic: About then Li Zongyi's wife in the same district, Lady Xia—given name Wanchang—was also from a scholar's family.

sentences.zh: 與女匿居後圃中，賊至，挾其女共投井死。

translations.literal: She hid with her daughter in the rear garden; when bandits came, she clasped her daughter and together they threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: She hid with her daughter in the back garden. When bandits arrived, she clasped the girl and they jumped into a well together.

sentences.zh: 秦閏夫妻柴氏，晉寧人。

translations.literal: Qin Run and his wife, Lady Chai, were natives of Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Run and his wife Lady Chai came from Jinning.

sentences.zh: 閏夫前妻遺一子尚幼，柴氏鞠如己出。

translations.literal: Run's first wife had left a son still young; Lady Chai reared him as her own.
translations.idiomatic: Run's first wife had left a young son, and Lady Chai raised him as her own.

sentences.zh: 未幾柴氏有子，閏夫病且死，囑柴氏曰：「我病不復起，家貧，惟二幼子，汝能撫其成立，我死亦無憾矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Lady Chai bore a son; Run fell gravely ill and was near death, and charged Lady Chai, saying, "My illness will not improve; the family is poor, and there are only these two young sons—if you can rear them to adulthood, I will die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lady Chai bore a son. Run fell mortally ill and told her, "I won't recover. We're poor, with only these two little boys. Raise them well and I'll die content."

sentences.zh: 閏夫死，家事日微，柴氏辛勤紡績，遣二子就學。

translations.literal: Run died; the family's circumstances daily declined, but Lady Chai toiled at spinning and weaving and sent both sons to study.
translations.idiomatic: After Run died the household grew poorer, but Lady Chai spun and wove tirelessly and put both boys in school.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，賊犯晉寧，其長子為賊驅迫，在圍中，既而得脫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, bandits attacked Jinning; the elder son was driven by the bandits and was in their midst, but later he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 18 bandits attacked Jinning. Their elder son was forced into service with the rebels but eventually escaped.

sentences.zh: 初在賊時，有惡少與張福為仇，往滅其家。

translations.literal: While he was initially with the bandits, a wicked youth bore a grudge against Zhang Fu and went to annihilate his household.
translations.idiomatic: While he was with the rebels, a young ruffian who hated Zhang Fu went to wipe out Zhang's family.

sentences.zh: 及官軍至，福訴其事，事連柴氏長子，法當誅。

translations.literal: When government troops arrived, Fu reported the affair; the matter implicated Lady Chai's elder son, and by law he should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops arrived, Zhang Fu reported it. The case implicated the elder son, who by law faced execution.

sentences.zh: 柴氏引次子詣官泣訴曰：「往從惡者，吾次子，非吾長子也。」

translations.literal: Lady Chai brought her younger son before the officials and wept in petition, saying, "The one who went with the wicked was my younger son, not my elder son."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chai brought her younger son to the magistrate in tears and claimed, "The son who followed the rebels was my younger boy, not the elder."

sentences.zh: 次子曰：「我之罪可加於兄乎！」

translations.literal: The younger son said, "How can my crime be laid on my elder brother!"
translations.idiomatic: The younger son cried, "How can my guilt be put on my brother!"

sentences.zh: 鞫之至死不易其言。

translations.literal: Under interrogation even unto death they did not change their words.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture to the point of death, neither changed their story.

sentences.zh: 官反疑次子非柴氏所出，訊之他囚，始得其情。

translations.literal: The officials instead grew suspicious that the younger son was not born of Lady Chai; questioning other prisoners, they finally learned the true facts.
translations.idiomatic: Officials doubted the younger son was really hers and questioned other prisoners until the truth came out.

sentences.zh: 官義柴氏之行，為之言曰：「婦執義不忘其夫之命，子趨死而能成母之志，此天理人情之至也。」

translations.literal: The officials honored Lady Chai's conduct and spoke on her behalf, saying, "The wife upheld righteousness and did not forget her husband's charge; the son rushed toward death and was able to fulfill his mother's intent—this is the utmost of heavenly principle and human feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Lady Chai's conduct, the magistrate declared, "The wife kept faith with her husband's dying charge, and the son faced death to fulfill his mother's wish—this is the highest expression of heaven's order and human devotion."

sentences.zh: 遂釋免其長子，而次子亦得不死。

translations.literal: Thereupon they released and exempted the elder son, and the younger son likewise was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: They released the elder son, and the younger was spared as well.

sentences.zh: 時人皆以為難。

translations.literal: People of the time all regarded this as hard to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries all considered this extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，有司上其事，旌其門而復其家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the local officials reported the matter upward, commended the family with a ceremonial arch over their gate, and restored their household [with tax and corvée relief].
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 officials reported the case to the court, which erected a commemorative arch over their gate and granted commendation and tax relief to the household.

sentences.zh: 也先忽都，蒙古欽察氏，大寧路達魯花赤鐵木兒不花之妻，以夫恩封雲中郡君。

translations.literal: Yesen Huddu, of the Mongol Qincha clan, was wife of Temür Buqa, darugachi of Daning Circuit, and by her husband's grace was enfeoffed as Lady of Yunzhong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yesen Huddu, a Qincha Mongol, was the wife of Temür Buqa, darugachi of Daning Circuit. Through her husband's privilege she was ennobled as Lady of Yunzhong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 夫坐事免官，居大寧。

translations.literal: Her husband, implicated in an affair, was removed from office and dwelt in Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband lost his post over a legal matter and lived in Daning.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，紅巾賊至，也先忽都與妾玉蓮走尼寺中，為賊所得，令與眾婦縫衣，拒不肯為。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, Red Turban bandits came; Yesen Huddu fled with the concubine Yulian to a nunnery, was captured by bandits, and was ordered to sew clothes with the other women—but refused.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 18 Red Turban rebels arrived. Yesen Huddu fled with her concubine Yulian to a nunnery but was captured and ordered to sew with other women. She refused.

sentences.zh: 賊嚇以刃，也先忽都罵曰：「我達魯花赤妻也，汝曹賊也，我不能為針工以從賊。」

translations.literal: The bandits threatened her with blades; Yesen Huddu cursed them, saying, "I am the wife of a darugachi—you lot are bandits—I cannot work as a seamstress and follow bandits."
translations.idiomatic: When they threatened her with blades, she cursed them: "I am a darugachi's wife—you're nothing but rebels. I won't stitch clothes for bandits."

sentences.zh: 賊怒殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels killed her in fury.

sentences.zh: 玉蓮因自縊者凡三，賊並殺之。

translations.literal: Yulian thereupon hanged herself as well; those who hanged themselves numbered three in all, and the bandits killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yulian hanged herself too. Three women had taken their own lives, and the bandits killed them all.

sentences.zh: 先是，其子完者帖木兒，年十四，與父出城，見執於賊。

translations.literal: Earlier, her son Wanzha Temür, fourteen years old, went out of the city with his father and was seized by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier her fourteen-year-old son Wanzha Temür had gone outside the city with his father and was captured by rebels.

sentences.zh: 完者拜哭，請以身代父死。

translations.literal: Wanzha bowed and wept, begging to die in his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzha bowed and wept, offering his own life for his father's.

sentences.zh: 賊愛完者姿秀，遂挈以從。

translations.literal: The bandits admired Wanzha's handsome appearance and took him along.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels admired his handsome bearing and took him away.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃獲脫歸，訪母屍並玉蓮葬焉。

translations.literal: After a long while he managed to escape and return, sought his mother's corpse, and buried her together with Yulian.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he escaped and returned, found his mother's body, and buried her together with Yulian.

sentences.zh: 呂彥能者，陵州人。

translations.literal: Lü Yanneng was a native of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yanneng came from Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，賊犯陵州，彥能與家人謀所往。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, bandits invaded Lingzhou; Yanneng and his family deliberated where to go.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 18 bandits attacked Lingzhou, and Yanneng and his family debated where to flee.

sentences.zh: 其姊久嫠居，寓彥能家，先曰：「我喪夫二十年，又無後，不死何為？

translations.literal: His elder sister, long widowed and staying at Yanneng's house, spoke first, saying, "I have mourned my husband twenty years and have no descendants—why not die?
translations.idiomatic: His widowed elder sister, who lived with him, spoke first: "I've been widowed twenty years with no heirs—what reason do I have to live?

sentences.zh: 苟辱身，則辱吾弟矣。」

translations.literal: If I were dishonored, I would disgrace my younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: If I were defiled, I'd disgrace my brother."

sentences.zh: 赴井死。

translations.literal: She went to a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 其妻劉氏語彥能曰：「妾為君家婦二十八年，茲不幸逢亂離，必不負君，君可自往，妾入井矣。」

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Liu, said to Yanneng, "I have been your family's wife twenty-eight years; now, unluckily meeting turmoil and separation, I will surely not fail you—go on yourself; I am going into the well."
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Liu told him, "I've been your wife for twenty-eight years. In this calamity I won't betray you—go save yourself. I'm going into the well."

sentences.zh: 彥能二女及子婦王氏、二孫女，皆隨劉氏溺井。

translations.literal: Yanneng's two daughters, his daughter-in-law Lady Wang, and two granddaughters all followed Lady Liu into the well and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yanneng's two daughters, his daughter-in-law Lady Wang, and two granddaughters followed Lady Liu into the well.

sentences.zh: 一門死者七人。

translations.literal: Seven persons of one household died.
translations.idiomatic: Seven members of the family died.

sentences.zh: 劉公翼妻蕭氏，濟南人，有姿色，頗通書史。

translations.literal: Liu Gongyi's wife, Lady Xiao, was a native of Jinan, fair in appearance, and well versed in books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongyi's wife Lady Xiao came from Jinan. Beautiful and well educated, she was versed in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，聞毛貴兵將壓境，豫與夫謀曰：「妾詩書家女，誓以冰雪自將，儻城陷被執，悔將何追？

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, hearing that Mao Gui's troops were about to press upon the border, she beforehand consulted with her husband, saying, "I am a daughter of a family of poetry and books; I have sworn to keep myself pure as ice and snow—if the city falls and I am seized, what regret could be undone?
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 18, hearing Mao Gui's army was about to overrun the region, she told her husband in advance, "I come from a literary family and have vowed to keep myself as pure as ice. If the city falls and I'm captured, it'll be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 妾以二子一女累君，去作清白鬼於泉下耳！」

translations.literal: Your wife burdened you with two sons and a daughter—[I] go to be a chaste ghost beneath the springs!"
translations.idiomatic: I've burdened you with two sons and a daughter—now I leave to be an unstained ghost in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 夫曰：「事未至，何急於此！」

translations.literal: The husband said, "The matter has not yet arrived—why such haste!"
translations.idiomatic: Her husband said, "It hasn't come to that yet—why rush into this!"

sentences.zh: 居亡何，城陷，蕭解絛自縊死。

translations.literal: Before long, the city fell; Xiao untied her sash and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell. Lady Xiao loosed her sash and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 袁氏孤女，建康路溧水州人，年十五。

translations.literal: An orphan girl of the Yuan clan, a native of Lishui Subprefecture in Jiankang Circuit, age fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: There was an orphan girl of the Yuan family from Lishui Subprefecture in Jiankang Circuit. She was fifteen years old.

sentences.zh: 其母嚴氏，孀居極貧，病癱瘓臥於床者數年，女事母至孝。

translations.literal: Her mother, Lady Yan, widowed and extremely poor, paralyzed and bedridden for several years; the girl served her mother with utmost filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Lady Yan lived in widowhood in dire poverty. Paralyzed, she had lain in bed for years, and the girl cared for her with the deepest filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，兵火延其里，鄰婦強攜女出避火，女泣曰：「我何忍舍母去乎，同死而已！」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng, war fire spread to their lane; a neighbor woman forcibly took the girl out to flee the fire. The girl wept and said, "How could I bear to leave my mother? Death together, nothing more!"
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 12, fighting and fire spread to their neighborhood. A neighbor woman forcibly dragged the girl out to escape the flames. The girl wept and said, "How could I abandon my mother? We die together, and that is all!"

sentences.zh: 遂入室抱母，共焚而死。

translations.literal: She then entered the room, embraced her mother, and they burned to death together.
translations.idiomatic: She went back inside, held her mother in her arms, and the two perished together in the flames.

sentences.zh: 徐允讓妻潘氏，名妙圓，山陰人。

translations.literal: Xu Yunrang's wife, Lady Pan, named Miaoyuan, was a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yunrang's wife Lady Pan, whose given name was Miaoyuan, came from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 至正十九年，與其夫從舅避兵山谷間。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhizheng, she and her husband followed their uncle to avoid troops in the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 19, she and her husband followed their uncle into the mountain valleys to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 舅被執，夫泣以救舅脫，夫被兵所殺，欲強辱潘氏。

translations.literal: The uncle was seized; the husband wept as he tried to save the uncle and get him free; the husband was killed by the soldiers, who wished to forcibly violate Lady Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Their uncle was captured. Her husband wept as he struggled to save him and win his release, but the soldiers killed him and then tried to force themselves on Lady Pan.

sentences.zh: 潘氏因紿之曰：「我夫既死，我從汝必矣。

translations.literal: Lady Pan therefore deceived them, saying, "My husband is already dead—I will certainly follow you.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pan deceived them, saying, "My husband is dead. I will surely go with you.

sentences.zh: 若能焚吾夫，可無憾也。」

translations.literal: If you can cremate my husband, I can be without regret."
translations.idiomatic: If you will cremate my husband, I shall have no regret."

sentences.zh: 兵信之，聚薪以焚其夫。

translations.literal: The soldiers believed her, gathered firewood, and burned her husband.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers believed her, piled up firewood, and burned her husband.

sentences.zh: 火既熾，潘氏且泣且語，遂投火以死。

translations.literal: When the fire was already blazing, Lady Pan weeping and speaking, then threw herself into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: Once the flames were roaring, Lady Pan wept and spoke as she went, then cast herself into the fire and died.

sentences.zh: 又諸暨蔡氏者，王琪妻也。

translations.literal: Also there was Lady Cai of Zhuji, wife of Wang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Cai of Zhuji, the wife of Wang Qi.

sentences.zh: 至正二十二年，張士誠陷諸暨，蔡氏避之長寧鄉山中，兵猝至，有造紙鑊方沸，遂投其中而死。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhizheng, Zhang Shicheng took Zhuji; Lady Cai fled to the mountains of Changning Township; soldiers arrived suddenly; there was a papermaking cauldron boiling—she threw herself into it and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 22, Zhang Shicheng captured Zhuji. Lady Cai fled to the mountains of Changning Township, but soldiers suddenly arrived. A papermaking vat was boiling nearby, and she threw herself into it and died.

sentences.zh: 趙洙妻許氏，集賢大學士有壬之侄女也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhu's wife, Lady Xu, was the niece of Academician Chancellor Youren of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhu's wife Lady Xu was the niece of Youren, Chancellor of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 至正十九年，紅巾賊陷遼陽，洙時為儒學提舉，夫婦避亂匿資善寺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhizheng, Red Turban bandits took Liaoyang; Zhu was then Confucian Schools Intendant; husband and wife hid from the chaos in Zishan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 19, Red Turban rebels captured Liaoyang. Zhu was then serving as Confucian Schools Intendant, and the couple took refuge from the turmoil in Zishan Temple.

sentences.zh: 洙以叱賊見害，許氏不知也。

translations.literal: Zhu was killed for rebuking the bandits; Lady Xu did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was killed for rebuking the rebels, but Lady Xu did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 賊甘言誘許氏，令指示金銀之處，許氏大言曰：「吾詩書冠冕故家，不幸遇難，但知守節而死，他皆不知也。」

translations.literal: The bandits with sweet words tempted Lady Xu, ordering her to point out where the gold and silver were; Lady Xu spoke loudly, saying, "I am from an old family of learning and official distinction; unfortunately encountering disaster, I only know to keep my chastity and die—I know nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to coax her with honeyed words and ordered her to show them where the gold and silver were hidden. Lady Xu answered in a ringing voice, "I come from an old family of letters and official rank. Misfortune has found us, but I know only how to keep my honor and die. I know nothing else."

sentences.zh: 賊以刃脅之，許氏色不變。

translations.literal: The bandits threatened her with blades; Lady Xu's expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: They threatened her with blades, but Lady Xu's face did not change.

sentences.zh: 已而知其夫死，因慟哭僕地，罵聲不絕口，且曰：「吾母居武昌，死於賊，吾女兄弟亦死賊，今吾夫又死焉。

translations.literal: When she then learned her husband had died, she wailed and collapsed to the ground, curses unceasing from her mouth, and said, "My mother lived in Wuchang and died at the hands of bandits; my sisters also died to bandits; now my husband has died as well.
translations.idiomatic: When she learned her husband was dead, she broke into wailing and fell prostrate to the ground, cursing without pause. She cried, "My mother lived in Wuchang and was killed by rebels. My sisters were killed by rebels too. And now my husband is dead as well.

sentences.zh: 使我得報汝，當醢汝矣。」

translations.literal: If I could repay you, I would mince you into paste!"
translations.idiomatic: If I could have my revenge on you, I would cut you to pieces!"

sentences.zh: 遂遇害。

translations.literal: She was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Then they killed her.

sentences.zh: 寺僧見許氏死狀，哀其貞烈，賊退，與洙合葬之。

translations.literal: The temple monks, seeing Lady Xu's death, pitied her chastity and martyrdom; when the bandits withdrew, they buried her together with Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: The temple monks, moved by the manner of Lady Xu's death and her steadfast virtue, buried her together with Zhu after the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 張正蒙妻韓氏，紹興人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhengmeng's wife, Lady Han, was a native of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhengmeng's wife Lady Han came from Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 正蒙嘗為湖州德清稅務提領。

translations.literal: Zhengmeng had once been Tax Affairs Intendant at Deqing in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengmeng had once served as intendant of tax affairs at Deqing in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 至正十九年，紹興兵變，正蒙謂韓氏曰：「吾為元朝臣子，於義當死。」

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhizheng, Shaoxing had a military mutiny; Zhengmeng said to Lady Han, "I am a subject of the Yuan dynasty; by righteousness I ought to die."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 19, troops mutinied in Shaoxing. Zhengmeng told Lady Han, "I am a subject of the Yuan dynasty. By duty I ought to die."

sentences.zh: 韓氏曰：「爾果能死於忠，吾必能死於節。」

translations.literal: Lady Han said, "If you can indeed die for loyalty, I can certainly die for chastity."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Han replied, "If you can truly die for loyalty, I can die for honor."

sentences.zh: 遂俱縊死。

translations.literal: They then both hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Then they hanged themselves together.

sentences.zh: 其女池奴，年十七，泣曰：「父母既死，吾何以獨生！」

translations.literal: Their daughter Chinu, age seventeen, wept and said, "My parents are already dead—how could I live alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Their daughter Chinu, seventeen years old, wept and said, "My parents are dead. How can I go on living alone?"

sentences.zh: 亦投崖而死。

translations.literal: She also threw herself from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: She too threw herself from a cliff and died.

sentences.zh: 又何氏者，處之龍泉縣季銳妻也。

translations.literal: Also there was Lady He, wife of Ji Rui of Longquan County in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady He, the wife of Ji Rui of Longquan County in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 因避兵於邑之繩門岩，賊至，何氏被執。

translations.literal: Fleeing troops to Shengmen Rock in the district, when bandits arrived Lady He was seized.
translations.idiomatic: She had fled the fighting to Shengmen Rock in the district, but when bandits arrived Lady He was captured.

sentences.zh: 欲污之，乃與子榮兒、女回娘投崖而死。

translations.literal: Wishing to defile her, she then with her son Rong'er and daughter Huiniang threw herself from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: When they tried to violate her, she took her son Rong'er and daughter Huiniang and leapt from the cliff to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 劉氏二女，長曰貞，年十九；

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Liu family: the elder was named Zhen, age nineteen;
translations.idiomatic: The Liu family had two daughters. The elder was named Zhen and was nineteen;

sentences.zh: 次曰孫，年十七。

translations.literal: the younger was named Sun, age seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: the younger was named Sun and was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 龍興人，皆未許嫁。

translations.literal: They were from Longxing; neither had yet been betrothed.
translations.idiomatic: They were from Longxing, and neither had yet been betrothed.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒寇龍興，其母泣謂二女曰：「城或破，置汝何所？」

translations.literal: Chen Youliang attacked Longxing; their mother weeping said to the two daughters, "If the city should fall, where shall I place you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang attacked Longxing, their mother wept and asked the two girls, "If the city falls, where can I keep you safe?"

sentences.zh: 二女曰：「寧死不辱父母也。」

translations.literal: The two daughters said, "Better to die than to disgrace our parents."
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters answered, "We would rather die than bring shame on our parents."

sentences.zh: 城陷，二女登樓，相繼自縊。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the two daughters ascended a tower and hanged themselves one after the other.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the two girls went up to a tower and hanged themselves, one after the other.

sentences.zh: 婢鄭奴，亦自縊。

translations.literal: The maid Zhengnu also hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Their maid Zhengnu hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 於同祖妻曹氏，茶陵人。

translations.literal: Yu Tongzu's wife, Lady Cao, was a native of Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tongzu's wife Lady Cao came from Chaling.

sentences.zh: 父德夫，教授湖、湘間，同祖在諸生中，因以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Her father Defu was a professor in the Hu and Xiang region; Tongzu was among the students, and so he gave his daughter to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Defu taught in the lake and Xiang region. Tongzu was one of his students, and Defu gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 至正二十年，茶陵陷，曹氏聞婦女多被驅逐，謂其夫及子曰：「是尚可全生乎！

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhizheng, Chaling fell; Lady Cao heard that many women were being driven off; she said to her husband and son, "Can one still preserve life in this!
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 20, Chaling fell. Hearing that many women were being seized and driven away, Lady Cao said to her husband and son, "How can anyone hope to survive this?

sentences.zh: 我義不辱身，以累汝也。

translations.literal: I, by righteousness, will not suffer my body to be shamed and burden you.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot let my body be dishonored and become a burden to you.

sentences.zh: 顧舅年老，汝等善事之。」

translations.literal: Look to your grandfather's old age—you all must serve him well."
translations.idiomatic: Your grandfather is old. You must take good care of him."

sentences.zh: 遂自剄死。

translations.literal: Thereupon she cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then she cut her own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 妾李氏驚，抱持之不得，亦引刀自剄，絕而復蘇，曰：「得從小君地下足矣。」

translations.literal: The concubine Lady Li, startled, tried to hold her but could not; she also drew a knife and slit her own throat; she lost consciousness and revived, saying, "It is enough to follow my mistress underground."
translations.idiomatic: The concubine Lady Li, alarmed, tried to hold her back but failed. She too drew a knife and cut her throat. She lost consciousness, then revived and said, "It is enough if I can follow my lady into the grave."

sentences.zh: 是夕死。

translations.literal: That evening she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died that same night.

sentences.zh: 李仲義妻劉氏，名翠哥，房山人。

translations.literal: Li Zhongyi's wife, Lady Liu, named Cuige, was a native of Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongyi's wife Lady Liu, whose given name was Cuige, came from Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 至正二十年，縣大饑，平章劉哈剌不花兵乏食，執仲義欲烹之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhizheng, the county suffered great famine; Pingzhang Liu Hala Buhua's troops lacked food; they seized Zhongyi intending to boil him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 20, the county was stricken by famine. The troops of Pingzhang Liu Hala Buhua had no food, so they seized Zhongyi and meant to boil him alive.

sentences.zh: 仲義弟馬兒走報劉氏，劉氏遽往救之，涕泣伏地，告於兵曰：「所執者是吾夫也，乞矜憐之，貸其生，吾家有醬一甕、米一斗五升，窖於地中，可掘取之，以代吾夫。」

translations.literal: Zhongyi's younger brother Ma'er ran to report to Lady Liu; Lady Liu hurried to save him, weeping and prostrate on the ground, telling the soldiers, "The one you have seized is my husband—I beg your pity; spare his life. In our house there is one jar of sauce and one dou and five sheng of rice buried in the ground; you may dig them up and take them in place of my husband."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi's younger brother Ma'er ran to tell Lady Liu. She rushed at once to save him, weeping as she fell prostrate before the soldiers. "The man you have seized is my husband," she pleaded. "Have mercy and spare his life. We have a jar of sauce and one dou and five sheng of rice buried in the ground. Dig them up and take them instead of my husband."

sentences.zh: 兵不從，劉氏曰：「吾夫瘦小，不可食。

translations.literal: The soldiers would not agree; Lady Liu said, "My husband is thin and small—not fit to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers refused. Lady Liu said, "My husband is thin and small. He is not fit to eat.

sentences.zh: 吾聞婦人肥黑者味美，吾肥且黑，願就烹以代夫死。」

translations.literal: I have heard that plump, dark women taste best; I am plump and dark—I wish to be boiled in his place and die for my husband."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that plump, dark-skinned women taste best. I am plump and dark. Boil me instead, and let me die in my husband's place."

sentences.zh: 兵遂釋其夫而烹劉氏。

translations.literal: The soldiers then released her husband and boiled Lady Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers released her husband and boiled Lady Liu instead.

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不哀之。

translations.literal: All who heard grieved for her.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it mourned for her.

sentences.zh: 李弘益妻申氏，冀寧人。

translations.literal: Li Hongyi's wife, Lady Shen, was a native of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongyi's wife Lady Shen came from Jining.

sentences.zh: 至正二十年，賊陷冀寧，申語弘益曰：「君當速去，勿以我婦人相累。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhizheng, bandits took Jining; Shen told Hongyi, "You should leave quickly—do not let me, a woman, hold you back.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 20, rebels captured Jining. Shen told Hongyi, "You must leave at once. Do not let me, a woman, drag you down.

sentences.zh: 若賊入吾室，必以妾故害及君矣。」

translations.literal: If bandits enter my chamber, they will surely harm you because of me."
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels enter our home, they will surely harm you because of me."

sentences.zh: 言訖，投井死。

translations.literal: Having spoken, she threw herself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When she had finished speaking, she threw herself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 弘益既免於難，再娶安氏。

translations.literal: Hongyi, having escaped disaster, remarried Lady An.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi survived the ordeal and later married Lady An.

sentences.zh: 居二歲而弘益以疾卒，安氏時年三十，泣謂諸親曰：「女子一適人，終身不改。

translations.literal: After two years Hongyi died of illness; Lady An was then thirty; weeping she told her relatives, "A woman marries once and does not change for life.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Hongyi died of illness. Lady An was then thirty. Weeping, she told her relatives, "A woman weds but once and keeps that bond for life.

sentences.zh: 不幸夫死，雖生亦何益哉！」

translations.literal: Unfortunate that my husband died—though I live, what use is it!"
translations.idiomatic: My husband is gone. What good is there in going on living?"

sentences.zh: 乃竊入寢室，膏沐薰裳，自縊於柩側。

translations.literal: She then stole into the bedroom, bathed and perfumed herself and scented her garments, and hanged herself beside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: She slipped into the bedchamber, washed and perfumed herself, dressed in fresh clothes, and hanged herself beside the coffin.

sentences.zh: 鄭琪妻羅氏，名妙安，信州弋陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Qi's wife, Lady Luo, named Miao'an, was a native of Yiyang in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qi's wife Lady Luo, whose given name was Miao'an, came from Yiyang in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，能暗誦《列女傳》。

translations.literal: Bright from childhood, she could recite the Biographies of Exemplary Women from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood, she could recite the Biographies of Exemplary Women by heart.

sentences.zh: 年二十，歸琪。

translations.literal: At age twenty she married Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty she married Qi.

sentences.zh: 琪家世宦族，同居百餘口，羅氏執婦道無間言。

translations.literal: Qi's family had been officials for generations; over a hundred persons lived together; Lady Luo practiced wifely conduct without a word of complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's family had served as officials for generations, and more than a hundred relatives lived under one roof. Lady Luo fulfilled her duties as a wife without a murmur of complaint.

sentences.zh: 琪以軍功擢鉛山州判官，羅氏封宜人。

translations.literal: Qi was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture for military merit; Lady Luo was enfeoffed as Yiren.
translations.idiomatic: For his military service Qi was promoted to assistant magistrate of Qianshan Subprefecture, and Lady Luo was granted the title Proper Person.

sentences.zh: 至正二十年，信州陷。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhizheng, Xinzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 20, Xinzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 羅氏度弋陽去州不遠，必不免於難，輒取所佩刀淬礪，令銛甚。

translations.literal: Lady Luo reckoned that Yiyang was not far from the prefecture and would surely not escape calamity; she took the knife at her belt, sharpened it, and made it very keen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Luo judged that Yiyang, so close to the prefectural seat, would not escape the coming disaster. She took the knife at her belt, whetted it, and honed it razor-sharp.

sentences.zh: 琪問何為，對曰：「時事如此，萬一遇難，為自全計耳。」

translations.literal: Qi asked what she was doing; she replied, "Times are such—if by chance we meet disaster, it is a plan to preserve myself."
translations.idiomatic: When Qi asked why, she answered, "These are desperate times. If the worst should happen, this is my way to preserve myself."

sentences.zh: 已而兵至，羅氏自刎死，時年二十九。

translations.literal: Before long troops arrived; Lady Luo cut her own throat and died; she was then twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the soldiers arrived. Lady Luo cut her own throat and died. She was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 周如砥女，年十九，未適人。

translations.literal: Zhou Rudi's daughter, age nineteen, had not yet been married.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Rudi's daughter was nineteen and not yet betrothed.

sentences.zh: 至正二十年，鄉民作亂，如砥與女避於邑西之客僧嶺，女為賊所執。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhizheng, local people rose in rebellion; Rudi and his daughter fled to Késēng Ridge west of the district; the daughter was seized by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 20, the local people rose in rebellion. Rudi and his daughter fled to Késēng Ridge west of the district, but the girl was captured by bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「吾未娶，當以汝為妻。」

translations.literal: The bandit said, "I am not yet married—I shall take you as my wife."
translations.idiomatic: The bandit said, "I have no wife. You shall be mine."

sentences.zh: 女曰：「我周典史女也，死即死，豈能從汝耶！」

translations.literal: The girl said, "I am the daughter of Zhou the District Recorder—if death, then death; how could I follow you!"
translations.idiomatic: The girl answered, "I am the daughter of Zhou the district recorder. If I must die, then die I shall. How could I ever follow you!"

sentences.zh: 賊遂殺之。

translations.literal: The bandit then killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit killed her.

sentences.zh: 如砥時為紹興新昌典史。

translations.literal: Rudi was then District Recorder of Xinchang in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Rudi was then serving as district recorder of Xinchang in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 狄恆妻徐氏，天台人。

translations.literal: Di Heng's wife, Lady Xu, was a native of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Di Heng's wife Lady Xu came from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 恆早沒，徐氏守節不再醮。

translations.literal: Heng died early; Lady Xu kept her chastity and did not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Heng died young, and Lady Xu kept her widowhood and did not marry again.

sentences.zh: 至正二十年，鄉民為亂，避難於牛囤山，為賊所執，驅迫以前。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhizheng, local people rebelled; she took refuge at Niutun Mountain; she was seized by bandits and driven forward under compulsion.
