translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 20, the local people rose in revolt. She fled to Niutun Mountain for safety, but bandits seized her and forced her onward.

sentences.zh: 徐紿之曰：「吾渴甚，欲求水一杯。」

translations.literal: Xu deceived them, saying, "I am very thirsty—I wish to fetch a cup of water."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu deceived them, saying, "I am terribly thirsty. Let me draw a cup of water."

sentences.zh: 賊令自汲，即投井而死，時年十八。

translations.literal: The bandits let her draw it herself; she immediately threw herself into the well and died; she was then eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits told her to draw it herself. She at once threw herself into the well and died. She was eighteen.

sentences.zh: 柯節婦陳氏者，長樂石梁人。

translations.literal: Chaste widow Lady Chen of the Ke family was from Shiliang in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: There was the chaste widow Lady Chen of the Ke family, from Shiliang in Changle.

sentences.zh: 至正二十一年，海賊劫石梁，其夫適在縣郭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhizheng, sea bandits plundered Shiliang; her husband happened to be at the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 21, sea raiders plundered Shiliang. Her husband happened to be at the county seat.

sentences.zh: 陳氏出避賊，道與賊遇，被執以行。

translations.literal: Lady Chen went out to flee the bandits; on the road she met them and was seized and taken along.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen went out to escape the raiders, but met them on the road and was seized and dragged away.

sentences.zh: 陳氏且行且罵，賊亂捶之，挾以登舟，罵不已，忽振厲自投江中。

translations.literal: Lady Chen cursed as she walked; the bandits beat her at random; they forced her aboard a boat; she kept cursing without cease; suddenly with fierce resolve she threw herself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen cursed them as she walked. The bandits beat her wildly, forced her onto a boat, and still she would not stop cursing. Suddenly she rallied her strength and threw herself into the river.

sentences.zh: 其父方臥病，見其女至，呼之不應，駭曰：「吾豈夢耶！」

translations.literal: Her father was then bedridden with illness; seeing his daughter arrive, he called to her but got no answer; horrified he said, "Am I dreaming!"
translations.idiomatic: Her father lay ill in bed. When he saw his daughter arrive, he called to her, but she did not answer. Horrified, he cried, "Am I dreaming?"

sentences.zh: 既而有自賊中歸者，言陳氏死狀，乃知其鬼也。

translations.literal: Then someone returned from among the bandits and spoke of Lady Chen's death—then they knew it was her ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward someone came back from among the bandits and told them how Lady Chen had died. Only then did they realize it had been her ghost.

sentences.zh: 明日屍逆流​​而上，止石梁岸傍。

translations.literal: The next day the corpse floated upstream and stopped beside the Shiliang shore.
translations.idiomatic: The next day her body floated upstream against the current and came to rest on the bank at Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 時盛暑，屍已變，其夫驗其背有黑子，乃慟哭曰：「是吾妻也！」

translations.literal: It was the height of summer; the corpse had already decomposed; her husband examined it and found a dark mole on the back; he wailed and said, "This is my wife!"
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of summer, and the body had already begun to decay. Her husband examined it, found a dark mole on her back, and wailed, "This is my wife!"

sentences.zh: 舁歸斂之。

translations.literal: They carried her back and prepared her for burial.
translations.idiomatic: They carried her home and laid her out for burial.

sentences.zh: 李馬兒妻袁氏，瑞州人。

translations.literal: Li Ma'er's wife, Lady Yuan, was a native of Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ma'er's wife Lady Yuan came from Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 至正二十二年，李病歿，袁氏年十九，誓不再嫁，以養舅姑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhizheng, Li died of illness; Lady Yuan was nineteen; she vowed not to remarry and to support her parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 22, Li died of illness. Lady Yuan was nineteen. She vowed never to remarry and devoted herself to caring for her parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 有王成者，聞袁氏有姿色，挾勢欲娶之，袁氏曰：「吾聞烈女不更二夫，寧死不失身也。」

translations.literal: There was a Wang Cheng who, hearing Lady Yuan was beautiful, used his power and wished to marry her; Lady Yuan said, "I have heard that a resolute woman does not take a second husband—better death than loss of chastity."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Wang Cheng, hearing that Lady Yuan was beautiful, used his influence to try to marry her. Lady Yuan said, "I have heard that a steadfast woman does not take a second husband. I would rather die than lose my honor."

sentences.zh: 遂往夫墓痛哭，縊死樹下。

translations.literal: She then went to her husband's grave, wept bitterly, and hanged herself beneath a tree.
translations.idiomatic: She went to her husband's grave, wept bitterly, and hanged herself beneath a tree.

sentences.zh: 王士明妻李氏，名賽兒，房山人。

translations.literal: Wang Shiming's wife, Lady Li, named Sai'er, was a native of Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiming's wife Lady Li, whose given name was Sai'er, came from Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 至正二十五年，竹貞軍至縣，李氏及其女李家奴皆被執。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Zhizheng, Zhuzhen's army reached the county; Lady Li and her daughter Li Jianu were both seized.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 25, Zhuzhen's army reached the county. Lady Li and her daughter Li Jianu were both captured.

sentences.zh: 士明隨至軍，軍怒逐之。

translations.literal: Shiming followed to the army camp; the army angrily drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: Shiming followed them to the camp, but the soldiers angrily drove him off.

sentences.zh: 李氏謂其女曰：「汝父既為軍所逐，吾與汝必不得脫。

translations.literal: Lady Li said to her daughter, "Your father has already been driven off by the army—you and I surely cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li said to her daughter, "Your father has already been driven away by the soldiers. You and I will surely not escape.

sentences.zh: 與其受辱，不若死。」

translations.literal: Rather than suffer disgrace, better to die."
translations.idiomatic: Better to die than to endure disgrace."

sentences.zh: 女曰：「母先殺我。」

translations.literal: The daughter said, "Mother, kill me first."
translations.idiomatic: The daughter said, "Mother, kill me first."

sentences.zh: 李氏即以軍所遺鐶刀殺其女，遂自殺。

translations.literal: Lady Li then used the ring-knife left by the soldiers to kill her daughter, and then killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li took the ring-knife the soldiers had left behind, killed her daughter with it, and then took her own life.

sentences.zh: 竹貞聞之，為之葬祭，仍書其門曰「王士明妻李氏貞節之門」。

translations.literal: Zhuzhen heard of it, performed burial rites for them, and moreover wrote on their gate: "The Gate of Chaste Integrity of Wang Shiming's Wife Lady Li."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuzhen heard of it, he had them buried and sacrifices performed, and wrote on their gate: "The Gate of Chaste Integrity of Wang Shiming's Wife, Lady Li."

sentences.zh: 有司上其事，為樹碑焉。

translations.literal: The officials reported the matter upward, and a stele was erected for them.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities reported the affair to higher officials, and a commemorative stele was erected.

sentences.zh: 陶宗媛，台州人，儒士杜思絅妻也。

translations.literal: Tao Zongyuan, a native of Taizhou, was the wife of the Confucian scholar Du Sijiong.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Zongyuan of Taizhou was the wife of the scholar Du Sijiong.

sentences.zh: 歸杜四載而夫亡，矢志守節。

translations.literal: Having returned to the Du household for four years, her husband died; she vowed to preserve her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Four years after marrying into the Du family, her husband died. She resolved to remain faithful and never remarry.

sentences.zh: 台州被兵，宗媛方居姑喪，忍死護柩，為遊軍所執，迫脅之，媛曰：「我若畏死，豈留此耶！

translations.literal: Taizhou suffered military attack; Zongyuan was then in mourning for her mother-in-law, enduring death to guard the coffin; she was seized by roving soldiers and threatened with coercion. Yuan said, "If I feared death, how could I have stayed here!
translations.idiomatic: When Taizhou came under attack, Zongyuan was in mourning for her mother-in-law, risking death to guard the coffin. Roving soldiers seized her and tried to force her. She said, "If I feared death, why would I still be here!

sentences.zh: 任汝殺我，以從姑於地下爾！」

translations.literal: Do as you will and kill me—I shall follow my mother-in-law in the underworld!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill me if you must—I shall join my mother-in-law in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 遂遇害。

translations.literal: She was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Then they killed her.

sentences.zh: 其妹宗婉，弟妻王淑，亦皆赴水死。

translations.literal: Her younger sister Zongwan and her brother's wife Wang Shu likewise all threw themselves into water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger sister Zongwan and her brother's wife Wang Shu also drowned themselves.

sentences.zh: 高麗氏，宣慰副使孛羅帖木兒妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Gaoli was the wife of Boluotiemuer, Vice Commissioner for Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gaoli was the wife of Boluotiemuer, Deputy Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至正二十七年十二月，其夫死於兵，謂人曰：「夫既死矣，吾安能復事人乎！」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-seventh year of Zhizheng, her husband died in warfare. She said to others, "My husband is already dead—how can I serve another man!"
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhizheng 27, her husband was killed in the fighting. She told those around her, "My husband is dead—how could I ever serve another man!"

sentences.zh: 乃積薪塞戶，以火自焚而死。

translations.literal: She then piled firewood to block the door and burned herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: She piled firewood to block the door and burned herself to death.

sentences.zh: 張訥妻劉氏，藍田人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ne's wife Lady Liu was a native of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ne's wife, Lady Liu, came from Lantian.

sentences.zh: 訥為監察御史，早卒，劉守志不二。

translations.literal: Ne served as Censor; he died early, and Liu preserved her resolve without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ne was an investigating censor. He died young, and Lady Liu remained steadfast in her devotion.

sentences.zh: 河東受兵，劉氏二子衡、衍俱以事出外，度不能自脫，遂與二婦孫氏、姚氏決死，盡發貲囊分給家人，婦姑同縊焉。

translations.literal: Hedong suffered military attack. Lady Liu's two sons Heng and Yan were both away on affairs; judging they could not escape, she resolved on death together with her two daughters-in-law Sun and Yao, emptied their purses to distribute to the household, and mother-in-law and daughters-in-law hanged themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong came under attack, Lady Liu's two sons Heng and Yan were both away on business. Convinced they could not escape, she and her daughters-in-law Lady Sun and Lady Yao resolved to die together. She emptied the family coffers and distributed everything to the household, then she and her daughters-in-law hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 有華氏者，大同張思孝妻，為貊高兵所執，以不受辱見殺。

translations.literal: There was a Lady Hua, wife of Zhang Sixiao of Datong, who was seized by Mo Gao's soldiers and killed for refusing to submit to disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hua, wife of Zhang Sixiao of Datong, was captured by soldiers under Mo Gao and killed for refusing to endure dishonor.

sentences.zh: 其婦劉氏，僵壓姑屍，大罵不已，兵並殺之。

translations.literal: His daughter-in-law Lady Liu, stiffly pressing upon her mother-in-law's corpse, cursed incessantly; the soldiers killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter-in-law Lady Liu lay pressed against her mother-in-law's body, cursing without cease, and the soldiers killed her as well.

sentences.zh: 後家人殮其屍，婦姑之手猶相持不捨。

translations.literal: Later the family prepared their corpses for burial; the daughter-in-law's and mother-in-law's hands still clasped each other and would not let go.
translations.idiomatic: When the family later prepared the bodies for burial, the hands of daughter-in-law and mother-in-law were still locked together and would not be parted.

sentences.zh: 觀音奴妻卜顏的斤，蒙古氏，宗王黑閭之女。

translations.literal: Guanyinnu's wife Buyandejin was of Mongol stock, daughter of the imperial clansman Heilü.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyinnu's wife Buyandejin was a Mongol, the daughter of the imperial clansman Prince Heilü.

sentences.zh: 大都被兵，卜顏的斤謂其夫曰：「我乃國族，且年少，必不容於人，豈惜一死以辱家國乎！」

translations.literal: When the capital suffered military attack, Buyandejin said to her husband, "I am of the imperial clan and still young—surely I shall not be spared; how could I begrudge one death to avoid disgracing family and state!"
translations.idiomatic: When the capital came under attack, Buyandejin said to her husband, "I am of the imperial clan and still young. They will surely show me no mercy. How could I cling to life and bring shame upon my family and my country!"

sentences.zh: 遂自縊而死。

translations.literal: She then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: She then hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 時張棟妻王氏語家人曰：「吾為狀元妻，義不可辱。」

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Dong's wife Lady Wang said to her family, "As the wife of a zhuangyuan, by propriety I cannot suffer disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Dong's wife Lady Wang told her family, "I am the wife of a zhuangyuan. By every principle of honor, I cannot endure disgrace."

sentences.zh: 赴井死。

translations.literal: She went to a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 其姑哭之慟，亦赴井死。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law wept in anguish and also threw herself into the well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law wept in anguish and also threw herself into the well and died.

sentences.zh: 安志道妻劉氏，順州人。

translations.literal: An Zhidao's wife Lady Liu was a native of Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Zhidao's wife, Lady Liu, came from Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 志道及劉氏之弟明理，並登進士第。

translations.literal: Zhidao and Lady Liu's younger brother Mingli both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Both An Zhidao and Lady Liu's younger brother Mingli passed the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 劉氏避兵匿巖穴中，軍至，欲污之，劉氏曰：「我弟與夫皆進士也，我豈受汝辱乎！」

translations.literal: Lady Liu hid from the troops in a mountain cave; when soldiers arrived and wished to violate her, Liu said, "My younger brother and husband are both jinshi—how could I accept your disgrace!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu hid from the troops in a mountain cave. When soldiers arrived and tried to violate her, she said, "My younger brother and my husband are both jinshi graduates. How could I submit to your dishonor!"

sentences.zh: 軍士以兵磨其體，劉大罵不輟聲，軍怒，乃鉤斷其舌，含糊而死。

translations.literal: The soldiers scraped her body with their weapons; Liu cursed loudly without cease; the army in anger then hooked out and severed her tongue, and she died with muffled sounds.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers scraped her body with their blades. Lady Liu cursed them without stopping. Enraged, they hooked out her tongue and cut it off; she died making inarticulate sounds.

sentences.zh: 宋謙妻趙氏，大都人。

translations.literal: Song Qian's wife Lady Zhao was a native of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qian's wife, Lady Zhao, was from the capital.

sentences.zh: 兵破大都，趙氏子婦溫氏、高氏，孫婦高氏、徐氏，皆有姿色，合謀曰：「兵且至矣，我等豈可辱身以苟全哉！」

translations.literal: When troops breached the capital, Zhao's daughters-in-law Wen and Gao and granddaughters-in-law Gao and Xu were all beautiful; they plotted together, saying, "The troops are about to arrive—how can we disgrace our persons merely to cling to life!"
translations.idiomatic: When the troops breached the capital, Lady Zhao's daughters-in-law Lady Wen and Lady Gao, and her granddaughters-in-law Lady Gao and Lady Xu, were all beautiful women. They agreed among themselves, "The soldiers are coming. How can we save our lives at the cost of our honor!"

sentences.zh: 趙即自經死，諸婦四人，諸孫男女六人，眾妾三人，皆赴井而死。

translations.literal: Lady Zhao immediately hanged herself; four daughters-in-law, six grandchildren male and female, and three concubines all threw themselves into the well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao immediately hanged herself. Four daughters-in-law, six grandchildren, and three concubines all threw themselves into the well and died.

sentences.zh: 齊關妻劉氏，河南人。

translations.literal: Qi Guan's wife Lady Liu was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Guan's wife, Lady Liu, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 關應募為千夫長，戰死澤、潞間。

translations.literal: Guan volunteered as a chiliarch and died in battle between Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan enlisted as a chiliarch and was killed in battle between Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 劉氏貧無所依，守志不奪。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was poor with none to rely upon, yet preserved her resolve undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: Left poor and without support, Lady Liu nonetheless held to her vow and would not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 有來強議婚者，劉氏紿曰：「吾三月三日有心願，償畢，當從汝所言。」

translations.literal: When someone came pressing to arrange a marriage, Lady Liu deceived him, saying, "On the third day of the third month I have a vow to fulfill; when it is fulfilled, I shall accede to what you propose."
translations.idiomatic: When a man came pressing her to remarry, Lady Liu put him off, saying, "On the third day of the third month I have a vow to fulfill. When it is done, I will do as you ask."

sentences.zh: 是日，徑往彰德天寧寺，登浮圖絕頂，祝天曰： 「妾本河南名家劉氏女，遭世亂，適湖南齊關為妻。

translations.literal: On that day she went straight to Tianning Temple in Zhangde, ascended to the top of the pagoda, and prayed to heaven: "I was originally a girl of the eminent Liu family of Henan; encountering world disorder, I was given in marriage to Qi Guan of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: On that day she went straight to Tianning Temple in Zhangde, climbed to the top of the pagoda, and prayed to heaven: "I was born a daughter of the eminent Liu family of Henan. In this age of chaos I was given in marriage to Qi Guan of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 今夫已死，不敢失節也。」

translations.literal: Now my husband is dead—I dare not fail in chastity."
translations.idiomatic: Now my husband is dead. I dare not break my vow of fidelity."

sentences.zh: 遂投地而死。

translations.literal: She then threw herself to the ground and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then threw herself from the pagoda and died.

sentences.zh: 王宗仁妻宋氏，進士宋褧之女也。

translations.literal: Wang Zongren's wife Lady Song was the daughter of the jinshi Song Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongren's wife Lady Song was the daughter of Song Xiang, who had passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 宗仁家永平。

translations.literal: Zongren's family was at Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zongren's family lived in Yongping.

sentences.zh: 永平受兵，宋氏從夫避於鏵子山。

translations.literal: Yongping suffered military attack; Lady Song followed her husband in taking refuge at Huazishan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongping came under attack, Lady Song fled with her husband to Huazishan.

sentences.zh: 夫婦為軍所虜，行至玉田縣，有窺宋氏色美，欲害宗仁者，宋氏謂夫曰：「我不幸至此，必不以身累君。」

translations.literal: The husband and wife were captured by the army; when they reached Yutian County, someone who coveted Lady Song's beauty and wished to kill Zongren—Lady Song said to her husband, "Having been brought to this plight, I shall surely not let my person implicate you."
translations.idiomatic: The couple were captured by the army. When they reached Yutian County, a man who coveted Lady Song's beauty and wished to kill Zongren—Lady Song said to her husband, "Fate has brought me to this pass. I will not let my body become your ruin."

sentences.zh: 言訖，遂攜一女投井死，時年二十九。

translations.literal: When she had finished speaking, she took a daughter with her and threw herself into a well to die. She was then twenty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: When she had finished speaking, she took a daughter with her and threw herself into a well. She was twenty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 王履謙妻齊氏，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Lüqian's wife Lady Qi was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lüqian's wife, Lady Qi, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 治家嚴肅，克守婦道。

translations.literal: She managed the household with austere discipline and steadfastly upheld the ways of a wife.
translations.idiomatic: She ran her household with strict discipline and faithfully upheld every duty of a wife.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，賊陷太原，齊氏與二婦蕭氏、呂氏及二女避難於趙莊石岩。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, bandits captured Taiyuan; Lady Qi, together with her two daughters-in-law Xiao and Lü and two daughters, took refuge at the stone cliffs of Zhao Village.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 18, rebels took Taiyuan. Lady Qi, her daughters-in-law Lady Xiao and Lady Lü, and her two daughters took refuge in the stone cliffs at Zhao Village.

sentences.zh: 賊且至，度不能免​​，顧謂二女曰：「汝家五世同居，號為清白，豈可虧節辱身以苟生哉！」

translations.literal: When the bandits were about to arrive, judging they could not escape, she turned and said to the two daughters, "Your family has lived together for five generations, famed as pure and upright—how can you fail in chastity and disgrace your persons merely to cling to life!"
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were about to arrive, convinced they could not escape, she turned to her two daughters and said, "Your family has lived together for five generations, renowned for its integrity. How can you stain your honor and disgrace yourselves merely to cling to life!"

sentences.zh: 長女曰：「吾夫已死，今為未亡人，得死為幸。」

translations.literal: The elder daughter said, "My husband is already dead; I am now a widow—to obtain death is fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The elder daughter said, "My husband is already dead. I am a widow now. To die would be a blessing."

sentences.zh: 呂氏曰：「吾為中書左丞之孫，義不受辱。」

translations.literal: Lady Lü said, "I am the granddaughter of a Left Vice Grand Councilor—by propriety I cannot suffer disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lü said, "I am the granddaughter of a Left Vice Grand Councilor. By every principle of honor, I cannot endure disgrace."

sentences.zh: 齊氏大哭，乃與二婦二女及二孫女，俱投岩下以死。

translations.literal: Lady Qi wept loudly, then she, her two daughters-in-law, two daughters, and two granddaughters all leapt from the cliffs to their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Qi wept aloud, then she, her two daughters-in-law, two daughters, and two granddaughters all leapt from the cliffs to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 王時妻安氏，名正同，磁州人，平章政事祐孫女也。

translations.literal: Wang Shi's wife Lady An, named Zhengtong, was a native of Cizhou and granddaughter of the Grand Councilor You.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi's wife Lady An, whose given name was Zhengtong, came from Cizhou. She was the granddaughter of Grand Councilor You.

sentences.zh: 至正十九年，時以參知政事分省太原，安氏從之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhizheng, Shi served as Vice Grand Councilor with delegated authority in Taiyuan, and Lady An accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 19, Wang Shi was assigned as Vice Grand Councilor to oversee Taiyuan province, and Lady An went with him.

sentences.zh: 二十年，賊兵寇太原，城陷，眾皆逃，安氏與其妾李氏同赴井死。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, bandit troops raided Taiyuan; the city fell, everyone fled; Lady An and her concubine Lady Li together threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, rebel forces assaulted Taiyuan. When the city fell and everyone fled, Lady An and her concubine Lady Li threw themselves into a well together and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈梁國夫人，諡莊潔。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, she was posthumously ennobled as Lady of Liang and given the posthumous title Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, she was posthumously granted the title Lady of Liang and given the honorific Zhuangjie, "Solemn and Pure."

sentences.zh: 徐猱頭妻岳氏，大都人。

translations.literal: Xu Youtou's wife Lady Yue was a native of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youtou's wife, Lady Yue, was from the capital.

sentences.zh: 兵入都城，岳氏告其夫曰：「我等恐被驅逐，將奈何？」

translations.literal: When troops entered the capital, Lady Yue told her husband, "We fear being driven out—what shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: When troops entered the capital, Lady Yue said to her husband, "We may be driven from our home. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 其夫曰：「事急，惟有死耳，何避也。」

translations.literal: Her husband said, "Matters are urgent—there is nothing but death. Why shrink from it?"
translations.idiomatic: Her husband said, "Matters are urgent. There is nothing left but death. Why shrink from it?"

sentences.zh: 遂火其所居，夫婦赴火以死。

translations.literal: They then set fire to their dwelling and husband and wife entered the fire to die.
translations.idiomatic: They set fire to their dwelling and walked into the flames together.

sentences.zh: 其母王氏，二女一子，皆抱持赴火死。

translations.literal: Her mother Lady Wang, two daughters, and one son—all embraced each other and entered the fire to die.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Lady Wang, along with two daughters and one son, held one another and walked into the fire to die.

sentences.zh: 金氏，詳定使四明程徐妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Jin was the wife of Cheng Xu of Siming, Detailed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jin was the wife of Cheng Xu of Siming, who held the rank of Detailed Reviser.

sentences.zh: 京城既破，謂其女曰：「汝父出捍城，我三品命婦，汝儒家女又進士妻，不可受辱。」

translations.literal: When the capital had fallen, she said to her daughter, "Your father has gone out to defend the city; I am a third-rank consort by title, and you are both a Confucian family's daughter and a jinshi's wife—you cannot suffer disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, she said to her daughter, "Your father has gone out to defend the city. I hold the rank of a third-grade consort, and you are both a scholar's daughter and a jinshi's wife. We cannot endure disgrace."

sentences.zh: 抱二歲子及女赴井死。

translations.literal: She took her two-year-old son and her daughter and threw herself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: She took her two-year-old son and her daughter and threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 汪琰妻潘氏，徽州婺源人。

translations.literal: Wang Yan's wife Lady Pan was a native of Wuyuan in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan's wife, Lady Pan, came from Wuyuan in Huizhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年二十八而琰卒，潘氏誓不他適，以其夫從兄之子元圭為後。

translations.literal: At twenty-eight Yan died; Lady Pan vowed not to marry another, and made her husband's first cousin's son Yuangui her heir.
translations.idiomatic: When she was twenty-eight, Wang Yan died. Lady Pan vowed never to remarry and adopted her husband's first cousin's son Yuangui as her heir.

sentences.zh: 元圭時始三歲，鞠之不啻己出。

translations.literal: Yuangui was then only three years old; she raised him no differently than if he were her own child.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was only three at the time, and she reared him as tenderly as if he were her own.

sentences.zh: 潘氏卒年六十二。

translations.literal: Lady Pan died at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pan died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 元圭之子良垕，有子燕山。

translations.literal: Yuangui's son Lianghou had a son Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui's son Lianghou had a son named Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 燕山卒時，妻李氏年二十四，無子，乃守志自誓，父母欲奪而嫁之，不聽。

translations.literal: When Yanshan died, his wife Lady Li was twenty-four, childless; she then vowed to preserve her chastity; her parents wished to force her into another marriage, but she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshan died, his wife Lady Li was twenty-four and had no children. She vowed to remain faithful. Her parents tried to compel her to remarry, but she refused.

sentences.zh: 燕山兄子惟德，娶俞氏，惟德早死，二子甚幼，俞氏守節辛勤，不墜家業。

translations.literal: Yanshan's elder brother's son Weide married Lady Yu; Weide died early, the two sons were very young; Lady Yu preserved her chastity with arduous effort and did not let the family estate fall into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshan's elder brother's son Weide married Lady Yu. Weide died young, leaving two very small sons. Lady Yu endured hardship to remain faithful and kept the family fortunes from collapsing.

sentences.zh: 故人賢汪氏之門，而稱曰三節。

translations.literal: Therefore people praised the virtue of the Wang clan's household and called them "Three Chaste Women."
translations.idiomatic: People therefore revered the Wang household for its virtue and called them the "Three Chaste Women."

sentences.zh: 同郡歙縣吳子恭之妻蔣氏，年二十八而夫亡，孀居五十年，年七十八卒。

translations.literal: In the same commandery, Wu Zigong's wife Lady Jiang of She County—at twenty-eight her husband died; she lived as a widow fifty years and died at seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the same region, Wu Zigong's wife Lady Jiang of She County lost her husband at twenty-eight, lived as a widow for fifty years, and died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，旌表門閭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, her gate and lane were honored with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 14, the authorities erected an official commendation at her home.
